definition: A VPN provides an encrypted connection over a network to reach private resources.
TLS encrypts the connection between a remote VPN client and its endpoint.
IPsec is the network encryption protocol suite used by Site-to-Site VPN.
A Client VPN endpoint terminates and manages remote client sessions.
CIDR notation describes an IP address range using an address and a prefix length.
Mutual authentication uses client certificates to authenticate VPN clients.
SAML enables federated user authentication through an identity provider.
An authorization rule grants selected users access to a destination network.
Split tunnel sends traffic matching configured VPN destination routes through the tunnel while other traffic uses local routing.
A security group controls which network traffic can reach a resource.
SNAT replaces the source IP address of outgoing traffic with another address.
An Availability Zone is a separate deployment location used for redundant VPN subnet associations.
